subject: move: a jump's verdict treats a rise over the walkable step (st.env.step, 45 cm) as a level change, not one over the step slack (step_tol 65). The pond bank's 61-63 cm hops were under 65, so 7 landings of the run legs on the top past the cell, going on forward (window 2026-11-19 00:15-00:26Z: feet_dz 1-43, off 65-195, nearest 49-107; jump_stats rule C 0 of 9) were judged on a walk point's 45 cm with no over/above credit, called "far" and re-planned. Now 46-64 cm jumps get jump_land_cm 130 and the over and above credits. Goalposts: inside the slack the height test (dz < 65) cannot tell the top from the foot, so for a level change of at most step_tol the feet must also be past half the rise from the takeoff's level toward the landing's (the over rule's own test) for within and above; rises over 65 and under 46 are judged as before. That also turns an old false landing into a miss: at the foot under the lip within 45 cm (the old rule called it landed). Tests (test_move): a 61 cm hop on the top 99 cm past the cell is landed (why=within, rise=61) and the plan goes on (lwp 3); 63 cm, 1.9 m on, nearest 107 and 61 cm, 1.8 m on, 42 cm over the top are landed why=over; back at the foot 60 cm short, at the foot under the lip, 99 cm past but 40 cm under the top, off the far side to the takeoff's level and 40 cm under it, and a 40 cm hop 99 cm past stay misses. On the old move.lua the three landings fail (why=far) and the under-the-lip foot is called landed; with the half-rise guard off, the three foot cases and the ford study's real miss 04:40:06Z (rise 55, feet at the takeoff's level, 94 cm off) are called landed. test_move, test_localplan, test_runner ALL OK; pytest -k "travel or jump" 40 passed. Run-up (not changed here, one change per window): the slow-down for a jump up (move.lua ~3558, `up` = rise > step_tol) keeps 65 for now and should not take the same step yet. The 61-63 cm hops pressed at 171-450 cm/s all came down on the top's level or higher past the cell (0 real falls back), so the misses were the judge, not the speed; slowing to under 100 cm/s for a 63 cm hump is not what a player does and costs the run. Revisit only if the relegged window shows rule C falls at 46-64 cm. Unseen row: `move: jump verdict=landed why=over ... rise=6x` (and why=within with rise 46-64) on the pond legs; far verdicts there from 7 to 0, no "jump landing missed; re-planning from here" after them, rule C falls stay 0.
